description: Stem slender and creeping, rooting at the nodes. Leaves round, long-stalked, slightly crenate, hairless, 15–25 mm across, peltate. Peduncles shorter than leaf-stalks. source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A hairless, slender perennial, 30–60 cm high. Leaves mostly basal, long-stalked, 35–50 mm across, palmatifid, with usually five wedge-shaped, toothed lobes, often themselves divided. Flowers pink or white, in small globular clusters, arranged in an irregular umbel. Bracts and bracteoles present. Calyx-teeth as long as the petals. Fruit round, covered with hooked bristles.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Marshes, fens, bog-margins and damp grassland; frequent.

source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Sandy shores; frequent although rather local.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A rigid, bushy perennial, 30–50 cm high, hairless and bluish-green. Leaves broad, very prickly, with conspicuous veins. Flowers pale blue, in very dense umbels interspersed with prickly bracts. Fruit covered with short spines, topped by the stiff, persistent calyx-teeth.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Hedges and road sides, mostly in the east and south-east; very rare and declining.

source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: purple or purple-spotted, 50–100 cm high. Leaves twice- or thrice-pinnate; leaflets rather blunt. Fruit 5–6 mm, 2–3 times as long as broad, slightly ridged.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Hedges and shady places; abundant except in parts of the west.

source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Erect perennial, 70–120 cm, hairy, especially in the lower part; stem stout, hollow, grooved. Leaves large, triangular, thrice-pinnate; segments pointed. Umbels terminal, long-stalked, with 8–12 rays. Bracts absent; bracteoles broad, deflexed, often pinkish. Fruit 6–8 mm, very smooth and shining, 3 times as long as broad.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Annual. Stem weak, hollow, hairless, 25–50 cm high. Leaves hairy, rather small, twice- or thrice-pinnate. Umbels small, shortly stalked, opposite the leaves with 3–6 rays. Bracts 0 or rarely 1. Fruit 2 mm, ovoid, covered, except for the beak, with hooked bristles.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Sandy banks and road sides near the sea, mainly from Lough Foyle to Waterford; rare.

source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A hairy annual, 15–50 cm high, with spreading branches. Leaves narrow, twice- or thrice-pinnate; segments linear. Umbels small, with 2 or 3 rays, or sometimes unbranched. Bracts absent; bracteoles about 5; fruit long, slender, consisting mainly of a long beak 3–4 times as long as the remainder.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Tilled fields; very rare, possibly extinct.

source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A hairy, aromatic perennial, smelling of aniseed; stem stout, hollow, grooved, branched, 60–100 cm high. Leaves large, twice- or thrice-pinnate, fern-like, flecked with white; leaflets toothed and pinnatifid. Umbels terminal, small, with 8–12 rays. Bracts absent; bracteoles 5–8, membranous, drooping. Flowers white. Fruit 15–20 mm, black, 3–4 times as long as broad, sharply ridged.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Road sides and waste-places; occasional in the north, extremely rare in the south. A former pot-herb.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A coarse, hairless biennial or perennial, 50–120 cm high, with hollow, grooved stems. Leaves shining, ternate or biternate, the upper ones with a strongly inflated sheathing stalk; leaflets oval, toothed 4–5 cm long. Flowers yellowish-green, usually hermaphrodite though sometimes male, in umbels with 8–12 rays; bracts absent, bracteoles very small. Fruit broadly ovoid, strongly ridged, with diverging styles.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Hedges, road sides and waste-places; locally abundant near the coast, rarer inland. Formerly cultivated for culinary use.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A hairless perennial, with a slender, smooth, often zig-zag stem 30–50 cm high, hollow after flowering, arising from a globular, deeply buried, underground tuber. Leaves few, mostly basal, triangular, mostly thrice-pinnate, withering early; upper stem-leaves twice-pinnate with almost linear leaf segments, with sheathing stalks. Umbels terminal, with 6–10 slender rays, drooping in bud; bracts very few or absent, bracteoles 2–5. Flowers small, white. Fruit 3–4 mm, ovoid-oblong, faintly ridged, with straight, almost erect styles.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Woods, heaths and pastures; very frequent.

description: Hairless or very minutely downy. Stem slender, solid, wiry, nearly smooth, 25–50 cm high. Leaves mostly basal, pinnate, with 4–7 pairs of toothed or pinnatifid, stalkless leaflets 15–20 mm long; upper stem-leaves usually finely dissected into numerous narrow segments. Flowers white in terminal umbels. Bracts and bracteoles absent. Fruit 2–2.5 mm, broadly ovoid.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Pastures and dry banks; frequent in the centre and south-east, rare elsewhere.

source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem hollow, brittle, ridged, hairless, often 1 m high. Leaves large, coarse. Leaflets usually 3–4 pairs, stalked, 25–60 mm long, irregularly toothed and lobed. Flowers white or pink.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Road sides and bushy places; locally frequent in parts of the south and west, absent elsewhere.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A hairless perennial with creeping rhizomes; flowering stems erect, hollow, grooved, up to 70 cm high. Fruit small, ovoid with long, downwardly curved styles.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Woods, gardens and waste-places, usually near houses; frequent in most districts. Formerly cultivated for medicinal and culinary use.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A hairless perennial with erect stems 1–2 m high. Leaves simply pinnate; leaflets large, 4–5 on each side, finely and regularly toothed. Umbels large, terminal, with about 25 equal rays; bracts and bracteoles conspicuous, often leafy. Flowers white. Fruit ridged, longer than broad.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A hairless perennial with erect stems 1–2 m high. Leaves simply pinnate; leaflets large, 4–5 on each side, finely and regularly toothed. Umbels large, terminal, with about 25 equal rays; bracts and bracteoles conspicuous, often leafy. Flowers white. Fruit ridged, longer than broad.

source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A hairless, slightly blue-greyish-green perennial 15–30 cm high. Stem solid. Leaves biternate or bipinnate ; leaflets linear, very fleshy, almost cylindrical, entire. Umbels terminal, on stout peduncles, with 10–20 equal stout rays. Bracts and bracteoles numerous. Flowers greenish-yellow; calyx-teeth absent; petals small, incurved. Fruit ovoid, spongy, ridged.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Seaside walls, rocks and cliffs. Frequent in most of the south, much rarer in the north.

source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Root club-shaped. Stem slender, thin-walled, 30–60 cm. Leaves long-stalked, the stalk much longer than the blade; upper leaves sub-erect, once-pinnate with 3–6 pairs of entire linear-oblong leaflets; lower leaves sometimes twice-pinnate. Umbels terminal, with 2–5 short stout rays; bracts 0, rarely 1, bracteoles several. Fertile flowers stalkless, the barren ones stalked. Fruit 3–4 mm, ovoid, somewhat flattened, with long (4–5 mm), rigid styles and calyx-teeth.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Canals and marshes; mainly in the east and centre; rare.

source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Roots with more or less cylindrical tubers developing from the base of the stem. Stem slender, solid or with a slight hollow when older, 30–80 cm high, ribbed. Lower leaves twice-pinnate with lanceolate leaflets, withering early; upper leaves pinnate to twice-pinnate, with linear leaf segments. Umbels terminal, with 7–12 slender rays. Bracts and bracteoles usually present. Pedicels not thickening in fruit. Fruit 2 mm, ovoid, styles about 1 mm.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Salt- and brackish marshes; frequent but local.

source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Roots with several rounded tubers 3–5 mm diameter developing some distance from the base of the stem. Stem solid, grooved. Lower leaves twice-pinnate, the segments lanceolate to ovate; upper leaf segments linear. Pedicels thickening in fruit. Fruit 3 mm, cylindrical, ribbed, styles about 3 mm, stout, erect.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Damp ground near the sea near Mullagh, Co. Clare and Cahersiveen, Co. Kerry.

source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem stout, hollow, grooved, 80–150 cm high. Sap, especially of roots, turning yellow on exposure to air. Flowers white or greenish-white; calyx-teeth rather short. Styles 2 mm, erect in fruit. Very poisonous.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: River sides, drains and canals; frequent in the south, east and north, rare in the centre and west.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem erect, hollow, grooved, stout, 50–120 cm high. Leaves twice- or thrice-pinnate; submerged leaflets narrow-linear or hair-like; aerial leaves oblong, usually pinnately-lobed, lanceolate to ovate. Umbels small, opposite the leaves, short-stalked, with 7–12 slender rays; bracts absent, bracteoles several. Flowers all stalked and hermaphrodite. Fruit 3–4 mm, narrowly ovoid .Calyx-teeth short.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: River sides, canals, drains and lake-margins; locally frequent in the centre and more common in the northern half, rare elsewhere.

source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem weak, submerged or floating, later erect, grooved, stout, 50–120 cm high. Segments of submerged leaves twice-pinnate, wedge-shaped, deeply incised. Calyx-teeth short.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Rivers and canals mainly in the centre; rare.

description: A dark green, hairless, annual. Stem hollow, slightly pale bluish-green (especially on larger plants), leafy, branched, 20–80 cm high. Bracts 0 or 1; bracteoles 3–5 on outer side of each partial umbel, long and directed downwards. Flowers white. Fruit ovoid, 3 mm, sharply ridged.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A hairless, aromatic perennial smelling of aniseed, up to 150 cm high. Stem stout, finely grooved, nearly solid. Leaves thrice-pinnate, with hair-like, yellowish-green leaflets. creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A hairless, leafy, unpleasant-smelling, very poisonous biennial, 100–150 cm high, with a smooth, hollow stem spotted with purple in the lower part. creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Biennial, smelling strongly of Celery, 30–70 cm high; stem hollow and grooved. Leaves pinnate or ternate; leaflets coarsely lobed and toothed. Umbels nearly stalkless, with 6–10 unequal rays; bracts and bracteoles absent. Flowers greenish-white. Fruit small (1.5 mm), round.
creator: Parnell, John
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description:
Four sub-species have been recorded from Ireland.
In subsp. erectum and subsp. microcarpum the mature fruit is dark brown or black above (paler below) and distinctly shouldered. In the former the shoulder is flat-topped and 4–6 mm at its widest point; the shoulder of the latter is more rounded and narrower (2.5–4.5 mm).
The uniformly pale-brown fruits of subsp. neglectum (2–4.5 mm) taper to the beak. Many of the similar but longer (4–7 mm) pale-brown subglobose fruits of subsp. oocarpum fail to mature.
Four sub-species have been recorded from Ireland.

source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: subsp. raphanistrum is an occasional weed of sandy or peaty fields; it is annual, usually with whitish flowers and fruits no more than 5 mm wide.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: subsp. maritimus (R. maritimus) is frequent on sandy and shingle shores, and very abundant in places; it is biennial with yellow (sometimes white) flowers and fruits more than 5 mm wide
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: The cultivated Radish is R. sativus
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A coarse, somewhat hairy annual or biennial with large, lyrate, pinnate leaves. Flowers 18–25 mm across; petals white or yellow, often with violet veins. Fruit indehiscent, deeply constricted between the seeds and eventually breaking at the constrictions, with a long, pointed beak at the apex.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: An erect, usually unbranched, hairy annual up to 50 cm high. Leaves pinnate or pinnately lobed, the upper more divided. Flowers pale yellow, about 7 mm across, the lower in the axils of leaf-like bracts. Fruits shortly cylindrical, spreading with an evident style [Fig. 82q].
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: June - August.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Road sides and waste-places in the south; spreading.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Native of Europe.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: An erect, sparsely branched or unbranched, somewhat bristly hairy biennial, up to 1 m tall, distinctive due to its large almost circular, flattened fruits over 2 cm across which, on opening, reveal a persistent and shiny septum. Lower leaves long stalked, ovate to cordate and sharply toothed upper similar but stalkless. Flowers whitish to purple about 2.5–3 cm across.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: May - September.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Widely scattered and fairly common garden escape, especially in the north and south, which can persist.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A small, erect, hairy annual. Leaves oblong, hairy, mostly in a basal rosette usually dead at flowering time; a few opposite or alternate on the stem. Flowers 15–20 mm across, in small cymes, opening in the morning and falling in the afternoon. Petals pale yellow, usually with a dark red patch at the base. Stigma 3-lobed, almost stalkless.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: June - August.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Dry, shallow, peaty soil overlying siliceous rock. Very local in the south-west and west (Cork to Mayo), mainly on the islands.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Leaves 10–15 mm long, oblong; stipules 2–3 mm. Petals bright yellow. Style longer than ovary.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: June - September.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Grassland overlying limestone; known only from one knoll in south-east Donegal, where it was first noted in 1893.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Leaves 5–8 mm long, oblong; stipules absent. Petals pale yellow. Style strongly curved, about as long as the ovary; stigma 3-lobed.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: May - July.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Limestone rocks in Clare and Aran Islands; locally frequent.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: All Irish material is thought to belong to subsp. piloselloides, a weakly defined sub-species with relatively large and sparsely hairy leaves. The distinctions between the sub-species are generally not clear, however, and the relationship of Irish plants to that of the same sub-species in the Pyrenees requires investigation.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: An erect, hairy perennial; stems up to 75 cm high, often spotted with purple. Lower leaves round or kidney-shaped, not deeply lobed; middle and upper leaves palmately lobed almost to the base; lobes pinnately divided, with linear-oblong segments. Flowers 4–5 cm in diameter; petals notched, pink or white. Carpels hairy.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: July - August.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Road sides and field-margins; frequent in the south-east, rare elsewhere.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A straggling or nearly erect perennial, sparsely hairy. Leaves palmately lobed, about a third of the way to the base. Flowers numerous, in axillary clusters. Petals 15 mm, bright reddish-purple. Carpels usually hairless.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: June - August.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Waste-places and road sides, usually near houses or ruins; frequent in the southern half, rather rare in the north.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A small herb, usually annual. Stems up to 50 cm, more or less prostrate, downy. Leaves round to kidney-shaped, with 5–7 shallow, crenate lobes. Flowers numerous, in axillary clusters; petals 10 mm, pale lilac. Carpels downy.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: June - September.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Road sides and waste-ground; occasional near the east coast, rare elsewhere.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A large, coarse, softly downy biennial; stems erect, up to 100 cm high, woody in the lower part, so that the plant is almost shrub-like. Leaves up to 10 cm across, nearly round, with usually 5 shallow, crenate lobes. Flowers in axillary or terminal panicles. Bracts of the epicalyx 3, united at the base, attached to the pedicel below the calyx, larger than the sepals and enlarging further in fruit. Sepals broadly triangular. Petals 10–15 mm, notched, overlapping, lilac-purple, with deep purple veins and base. Carpels downy.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: July - September.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Native on maritime rocks and bare ground near the sea; occasional but local. Also as an escape from gardens, usually near the coast.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Recent molecular evidence suggests that Lavatera may be better amalgamated with the genus Malva, with the above species thus becoming Malva arborea; however, we have decided to keep the genera separate for the time being.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: An erect, branched perennial, 50–100 cm high, covered with velvety down. Leaves broadly oval, often 3-lobed, toothed. Flowers in terminal racemes. Bracts of the epicalyx about 8, narrowly triangular, 5–7 mm long, free, inserted on the pedicel. Sepals ovate, pointed, slightly longer than the bracts. Petals 20 mm, scarcely notched, pale lilac-pink. Carpels downy.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: August - September.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Damp places by the south and west coasts, usually near houses; occasional.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem usually unbranched, erect and stiff, 50–100 cm high. Leaves narrowly lanceolate, entire. Pedicels about the same length as the yellowish-green flowers. Sepals usually 4; petals 4 or 5, the upper ones larger and deeply divided; stamens usually 20–25. Capsule nearly globular.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: June - August.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Road sides, sandy waste-ground, quarries and dry gravelly places; frequent throughout.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem usually branched, almost bushy, 30–50 cm high. Leaves ternately or pinnately divided, with linear segments. Pedicels longer than the yellowish-green flowers. Sepals and petals 6, sometimes 5; the upper petals variously divided. Stamens usually 15–20. Capsule oblong.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: June - August.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Sandy and gravelly ground usually near the coast mainly in the eastern half; rare.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A large tree with spreading branches; bark smooth and grey at first, but scaling on old trunks. Winter buds greenish. Leaves 8–15 cm, about as broad as long, cordate at the base, with 5 acute, coarsely toothed lobes. Flowers in long, drooping, catkin-like panicles, appearing with or after the leaves. Wings of fruit diverging at rather more than a right angle..
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: April - June.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Woods, hedges and waste-ground; abundant
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Native of central and southern Europe.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A. campestre, the Field maple, a fair-sized tree, but usually seen as a shrub; is occasionally planted in hedges and rarely naturalised. It has smaller leaves, with obtuse, entire lobes, the flowers are in erect panicles, and both wings of the fruit lie in the same straight line and the older twigs are ridged.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A. platanoides, the Norway maple, is often planted and is naturalised in woods and hedges in a few places. It has leaves like those of A. pseudoplatanus, but with finely pointed lobes and milky sap in the leaf-stalk. The yellowish flowers in erect panicles appear before the leaves and the buds are reddish.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A large, broad-headed, deciduous tree with scaling bark. Buds large, very sticky in spring. Leaves opposite, palmate, with 5–7 leaflets up to 20 cm long. Leaf-scars with a characteristic pattern suggestive of a horse-shoe. Flowers in erect panicles. Calyx tubular, 5-lobed; petals 4 or 5 (if 5 then one is often much smaller), white with pink or yellow spots; stamens usually 7; ovary superior, 3-celled. Fruit a large, spiny, leathery capsule with 1–2 large brown seeds.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: April - June.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Planted for ornament and occasionally self-sown in hedges and woodland.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Native of Europe.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Very large tree to 40 m with orange or yellowish or greyish bark. Young leaves becoming orbicular; adult lanceolate. Flowers more or less stalkless. Fruit bowl-shaped with the valves clearly protruding from the top, 9–13 mm across.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: July - September.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Planted for forestry in a few areas and now self-seeding.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Native of Australia.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Very large tree with whitish or greyish bark, up to 40 m high. Young and adult leaves lanceolate. Flowers more or less stalkless. Fruit bowl-shaped with the valves clearly protruding from the top, up to 9 mm across, smooth.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: July - September.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Planted for forestry in a few areas and now self-seeding.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Native of Australia.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Moderately sized tree up to 12 m high with greyish or yellowish-brown bark. Young leaves orbicular; adult lanceolate. Flowers with distinct pedicels up to 4 mm long. Fruit urn-shaped with the valves hidden, 8–10 mm across.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: July - September.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Planted for forestry in a few areas and now self-seeding.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Native of Australia.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Shrub or small tree up to 10 m tall with all leaves oval, sharply pointed, opposite; flowers with white or pale-pinkish, curved petals and a dark purple, globose berry.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: July - September.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Planted in large gardens and demesnes and self-seeding in a number of localities in the south-west.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Native of South America.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A bushy shrub with brownish, eventually peeling bark and hairless, opposite, stalked, oval, toothed leaves; young stems often reddish. Flowers axillary, drooping, 3–4 cm across. Calyx crimson, 4-lobed; petals 4, deep purple, shorter than calyx lobes. Stamens 8, very long. Fruit a blackish, fleshy berry.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: July - September.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Planted for hedges mainly in the west.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Native of South America.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: The variety most commonly planted, with fat, nearly spherical buds (‘Riccartonii’), hardly ever sets fruit and is naturalised only occasionally. Other forms, with narrower buds, are planted in a few districts and are becoming naturalised.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: 25–50 cm. high. Leaves usually slightly downy, not shining, somewhat triangular, very feebly toothed. Flowers 7–10 mm across; pedicels covered with glandular hairs. Fruit 2-seeded, drooping, covered with hooked bristles.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: June - August.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Woods, shaded road sides and as a garden weed; frequent.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: In some Irish plants the leaf-stalks appear almost equally pubescent all-round, but in many cases the leaf-stalks are more densely hairy on the upper surface. Further investigation of Irish plants is required.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Similar to C. lutetiana but with leaves slightly cordate, thinner, somewhat shining and more strongly toothed, with fruit nearly always not ripening.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: June - September.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Rocky and shaded places in northern half (north of a line running between Sligo and Dundalk); rare.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A hybrid between C. lutetiana and C. alpina; the latter does not now occur in Ireland, but probably did in the past.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stems erect, 100–150 cm. Leaves hairy. Hairs on green parts of stem lacking red bulbous bases (though red-based on red parts of stem). Petals 1.5–3 cm. Sepals entirely green.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: July - September.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Waste-ground, road sides and sand-dunes; rare.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Native of Eurasia.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem erect, 40–150 cm, with long stiff hairs with red bulbous bases even on green parts of stem. Leaves hairy. Petals 3–5 cm. Sepals red-striped or entirely red.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: July - September.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Similar situations; rare
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Native of North America.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Nearly hairless; stem unbranched 80–150 cm high. Leaves alternate, narrowly lanceolate, shortly stalked. Flowers deep purple-red, 25 mm across, in long terminal leafless racemes. Sepals almost linear and usually a deeper purple then the petals. Petals entire; upper two larger than the lower pair. Stigma 4-lobed.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: July - August.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Very rare as a native in rocky places in mountains; locally frequent as an introduction on bog margins, railway sidings, road sides and waste-ground in cities; less frequent in the westernmost third of the country.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Now commonly accepted as distinguished from Epilobium on the basis of molecular and morphological features, including its alternate leaves, slightly zygomorphic flowers, individual pollen grains and absence of an extension of the base of the flower (= hypanthium) above the base of the ovary.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stems stout, 80–150 cm high, branched. Whole plant softly hairy with obviously long spreading hairs. Leaves mostly opposite, stalkless, almost clasping the stem, oblong-lanceolate, toothed. Flowers deep rose-pink, c. 20 mm across; stigma 4-lobed.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: July - August.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Ditches, river and stream sides and other damp places; occasional in drier habitats; very frequent.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem 30–90 cm high, more or less softly hairy with somewhat tangled, long spreading hairs. Leaves oblong-lanceolate, stalkless, slightly toothed or nearly entire, some alternate. Flowers pale pink, 8–10 mm across; stigma 4-lobed.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: July - August.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Ditches, river and stream sides and other damp, often disturbed, places; very frequent.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem 15–60 cm high, creeping by stolons, slightly downy, the hairs mainly short and ± curled and appressed. Leaves hairless, oval-lanceolate, toothed, mostly opposite, at least the basal with a distinct stalk. Flowers pinkish mauve, 8 mm across; stigma 4-lobed. Buds slightly drooping.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: June - August.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Waste-ground in cities, road sides, hedgerows, woods and as a garden weed; very frequent
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem erect, branched, 30–60 cm high, with 2 or 4 longitudinal ridges running down from the bases of the leaves; short and leafy stolons formed above and below ground in summer. Leaves mostly opposite, stalkless, oblong-lanceolate, toothed, hairless. Buds erect. Flowers pale purplish-pink, 6–8 mm across, petals slightly lobed; stigma entire. Developing capsule with a few glandular hairs [Fig. 76c ].
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: July - August.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Marshes and damp waste-places; also on rocks and walls by rivers; frequent but less frequent in the centre and central-west .
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Similar to E. obscurum, but stem cylindrical, without ridges; stolons at base long and thread-like, often underground; leaves linear-lanceolate and occasionally with a very short stalk; flowers only 5 mm across and buds drooping.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Flowering: July - August.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Stem 60–120 cm, stiff, with many sub-erect flowering branches and 4 longitudinal ridges (2 in lower part) running down from the leaves; hairless and reddish below, with both curled and ± appressed hairs and spreading glandular hairs above. Leaves mostly opposite, oblong-lanceolate with an acute tip, a subcordate shortly-stalked base and a hairless finely-toothed margin. Flowers 4–5 mm wide, numerous; petals pale pink with darker margins, deeply cleft. Stigma entire. Young capsule with both curled and ± appressed and glandular hairs [Fig. 76d ], hairless later, 4–6 cm. Seed with a pale translucent beak below the hair-tuft.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: Waste-ground in cities, gardens and on road sides. Frequent, especially east of a line running between Coleraine and Kenmare; still spreading.

description: Stem 20–50 cm stiff, with appressed, silky non-glandular hairs above, hairless below with 4 lines running down from the leaves, downy above with appressed hairs; forming almost stalkless leaf-rosettes in autumn. Leaves 4–6 cm × 6–9 mm, strap-shaped, blunt at tip, almost stalkless, decurrent, hairless. Flowers 6–8 mm, lilac-pink, slightly notched. Young capsule with short crisped hairs but lacking glandular hairs, 7–10 cm long when mature [Fig. 76e ].
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A stiff, erect, usually shortly hairy perennial up to 1 m high. Leaves opposite or in whorls of 3, stalkless, lanceolate, 5–10 cm long. Flowers in dense, reddish-purple whorls in terminal spikes. Calyx with twice as many teeth as petals, the narrowly triangular teeth alternating with the rounded. Petals usually 6. Stamens twice as many as petals of two distinct lengths in any one flower. Ovary deeply sunk in the calyx-tube but free from it.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.

description: A creeping, hairless annual, forming small tufts. Leaves opposite, oval, 10–15 mm long, stalked at the base. Flowers very small, stalkless, axillary and numerous. Calyx 12 toothed; the broadly teeth triangular alternating with the linear. Petals 6, small, purple, sometimes absent. Stamens 6. Top of ovary overtopping the calyx.

description: A delicate annual, with very slender, erect stems up to 15 cm high, usually forked above. Leaves 5–10 mm, narrowly oval, opposite. Flowers 6–8 mm across. Sepals narrow, acute; petals 4 mm × 2 mm, white.

description: A deciduous shrub with green, 4-angled twigs. Leaves opposite, oval, acute, shortly stalked, entire or minutely toothed. Flowers 8–10 mm across, in small, axillary cymes. Sepals, petals and stamens 4. Petals free, pale green. Ovary 4-celled, superior, square in face-view. Fruit a somewhat fleshy 4-lobed capsule, bright pink, splitting to expose the orange arils, in each of which a seed is enclosed.

description: An erect, hairless perennial, 15–40 cm high, with long-stalked, entire, heart-shaped basal leaves. Stem with a single stalkless leaf. Flowers 20–25 mm across, solitary. Sepals slightly united at the base. Petals free, white, with translucent veins, slightly notched at the tip. Stamens 5, alternating with 5 staminodes; these have a broad, white base, divided above into about 12 slender branches, each ending in a greenish-yellow gland. Ovary 1-celled; stigma 4-lobed, stalkless. Fruit a capsule.
source: Parnell J., Curtis T. & Cullen E. 2012. Webb’s an Irish Flora. [8th ed.] Cork: Cork University Press.
